hints: Let X be the weight of an orange: X ~ N(131, 54^2).
An orange is large if its weight is at least 184 grams.
Find the upper tail probability: P(X >= 184) = 1 - Phi(0.9815) = 1 - 0.8368 = 0.1632, then convert to a percentage.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Define the normal model and parameters:
Let $X$ denote the weight, in grams, of an orange.
$$X \sim \operatorname{N}(\mu, \sigma^2) = \operatorname{N}(131, 54^2)$$
where $\mu = 131\text{ g}$ and $\sigma = 54\text{ g}$.

Step 2: Identify the condition for a large orange:
An orange is classified as large if $X \ge 184\text{ g}$.

Step 3: Standardise using Z = (X - mu) / sigma:
$$z = \frac{184 - 131}{54} = \frac{53}{54} = 0.98148... \approx 0.9815$$

Step 4: Find the upper tail probability:
$$P(X \ge 184) = P(Z \ge 0.9815) = 1 - \Phi(0.9815)$$
From the standard normal cumulative distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.98) = 0.8365, \quad \text{difference for } 1 = 3, \quad \text{difference for } 2 = 5$$
$$\Phi(0.9815) \approx 0.8368$$
$$P = 1 - 0.8368 = 0.1632$$

Step 5: State the final percentage:
$$\text{Percentage} = 0.1632 \times 100\% = 16.32\% \approx 16.3\%$$
(Cambridge accepts $16.3\%$ to $16.4\%$).

hints: 20% of oranges are small, so the greatest weight w of a small orange satisfies P(X < w) = 0.20.
Find the critical value from the standard normal table for a lower-tail area of 0.20: Phi(-z) = 0.20 => Phi(z) = 0.80, giving z = -0.842.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Set up the percentile condition:
Small oranges constitute the lightest $20\%$ of all oranges.
Let $w$ be the upper boundary (greatest possible weight) of a small orange:
$$P(X < w) = 0.20$$
where $X \sim \operatorname{N}(131, 54^2)$.

Step 3: Find the negative critical z-score:
Because the probability is less than $0.5$, the boundary lies to the left of the mean:
$$P(Z < -z_0) = 1 - \Phi(z_0) = 0.20 \implies \Phi(z_0) = 0.80$$
From the standard normal percentage points table:
$$z_0 = 0.8416 \implies Z = -0.8416 \approx -0.842$$

Step 4: Set up the linear equation for w:
$$\frac{w - 131}{54} = -0.8416$$

Step 5: Solve for w:
$$w = 131 + 54(-0.8416) = 131 - 45.4464 = 85.5536... \approx 85.5\text{ g}$$
(Cambridge accepts any value in $85.5 \le w \le 85.6$ grams).
